summary.intent: Execute all plans for GSD phase 68.1 (wiring CipherBox's v2.0 web app onto the node/v3 read+write chain) via wave-based parallel subagent orchestration, drive the phase through repeated verification-gap-closure cycles until the full 208-spec web-e2e suite passes, and incorporate live user bug reports and a product decision (GAP-6 backfill retirement/redesign) along the way.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.1 executed across 33 plans over multiple gap-closure rounds (14 initial + 8 + 7 + 3 further gap plans), fixing dozens of real production bugs (write-plane cold-load recovery, move write-link re-homing, batch-upload missing WriteChildRefs, shared single-file editor, kind-cache races, TEE republish enrollment, GAP-6 dead-code removal). Round-3 verification landed at 4/5 with the closing suite run still pending final tally when the transcript ends; two gaps (recovery.html v2-only, rotation-durability SC-4) were explicitly deferred by user decision.

repo: CipherBox node/v3: SealedChildRef (read plane, keyed by ipnsName) vs WriteChildRef (write plane, keyed by node UUID childId) — write-capability must always be resolved/keyed by UUID, never the ipnsName-based caller handle (bit multiple agents nearly got wrong, e.g. plan 68.1-31's moveItem fix).

TEE republish enrollment requires BOTH encryptedIpnsPrivateKey AND keyEpoch on POST /ipns/publish; omitting either means the record silently never gets enrolled in ipns_republish_schedule and dies at IPNS TTL.

Local dev mock-ipns-routing (:3001) keeps IPNS records in an in-memory Map — any container restart wipes it; records only survive via the API's synchronous ipns_records DB-cache write at publish time.

mock-ipns-routing's healthcheck used busybox wget against 'localhost', which resolves to ::1, but the app binds IPv4-only — perpetual 'unhealthy' status was a healthcheck bug, not a service failure; fixed to 127.0.0.1 in docker-compose.yml.
API runs on :3000, not :3001 (that's the delegated-routing mock) — easy to misdiagnose stack health against the wrong port.

dfsFindFolder in client.ts unconditionally re-resolved and overwrote already-loaded ancestor folderTree entries on every call, contradicting its own 'cheap on later calls' docstring — root cause of breadcrumb/navigation flicker (fixed in 68.1-26 with a cache short-circuit).

SharedWriteContext has no ipnsPrivateKey field — shared-write ops derive the publish key from inside the unsealed write-body itself, so subfolder writes only need a real writeKey recovered, not full key derivation (narrowed the 68.1-30 fix).

shares table's plaintext item_name column was dropped entirely (not renamed) by migration ApiSchemaCutover, making REQ-4's itemName backfill permanently dead code — reviving plaintext storage would violate the zero-knowledge rule; the redesign path is the already-partially-shipped item_name_encrypted/ECIES pipeline.
Decision-coverage gate parser requires the ID and any tag in the SAME bold markdown group: '- **D-04 [informational]:**' works, '- **D-04:** [informational]' does not.

Full web-e2e suite is describe.serial per file — an early failure aborts the rest of that file, so raw failure counts drastically understate real breakage; a file failing early can mask 30+ untested specs behind it.

code.finding: moveItem re-linked the read-plane SealedChildRef on move but left the WriteChildRef orphaned in the source folder's write-body, permanently breaking edit/save after a move; fixed in 68.1-31 by unsealing under source writeKey (keyed by resolved node UUID, not the ipnsName-based childId param), dropping from source, and re-sealing under dest writeKey with dest-before-source publish order preserved.

downloadFromIpns fed the parent folderKey into sdk-core's resolveFileMetadata, which requires the file's own readKey — silent type coincidence (both Uint8Array) caused AEAD decrypt failures surfaced as 'Decryption failed' in the text editor; fixed by recovering the file readKey via unsealChildReadKey before the call.

MAX_RETRIES/RETRY_DELAY_MS bumped from 3/2000ms to 8/3000ms to fix cold-reload subfolder navigation timeouts (GAP-2); the fast-load path itself (targetFolder?.isLoaded) was traced and found correct, not the culprit.

folder:loaded/folder:updated SDK-event handler needed an empty-children guard (don't let an empty-children event clobber an already-loaded non-empty folder) plus later a sequence-aware hybrid kind-resolution path (sync when cache warm, await resolveKinds on cache miss) to fix an owner-side kind-cache race blocking writable-shares 10.4.
Hardcoded isFolder = true meant the D-02 kind cache populated by 68.1-14 was never consulted in the shared browser, causing files to render/behave as folders; fixed in 68.1-15.

workflow: Long-running background e2e suites launched by a subagent are prone to 'lost wake' — the agent parks waiting on its own background shell and never gets re-invoked when it finishes, and its transcript can get evicted; mitigate with an independent disk-based watchdog (e.g. polling a .last-run.json mtime) plus prompt-based SendMessage resume while the transcript is still warm, falling back to a fresh continuation agent with explicit completed_state when evicted.

Session/quota limits can kill an agent mid-task after it already wrote artifacts to disk (a PLAN.md or partial commits) — recover by spot-checking disk state, validating what exists, and resuming inline rather than re-running from scratch.

Committing via `timeout 180 git commit` can report a false failure due to 1Password gpg-sign integration timing out even though the commit lands — always verify via `git log -1` before assuming a commit failed and retrying.

Worktree-isolated subagents self-report expected_base in their completion metadata, but this can be wrong (misreporting their own HEAD instead of the fork point) — verify the true fork base via `git merge-base` before recording it in the wave manifest.
Full monorepo/parallel test runs must never be launched from parallel subagents — scope post-merge gates to sdk/sdk-core only, and run any full-suite validation centrally/sequentially.

A live full 208-spec e2e run only proves the code green at the exact HEAD it ran against — fixes committed after the run started must trigger a fresh confirmation run before a phase-completion decision, not be assumed folded in.

User-facing spot-checks (asking to run a spec in headed mode, live bug reports while a suite runs) surface real regressions that automated e2e coverage structurally cannot reach yet (serial-abort shadowing) — treat user skepticism about 'still very broken' as a signal to verify against disk/logs, not dismiss.

friction: Two separate 'lost wake' incidents where the exit-gate agent launched a background e2e run and never got re-invoked on completion, requiring manual disk investigation and prompt-based resume both times.
Orchestrator's own `tail`/pipe masked a real non-zero exit code from a post-merge test gate, causing a false-green read that was only caught by re-running with proper exit-code capture.
Decision-coverage gate parser errors were opaque ('could-not-parse') and required reading the parser source (decisions.cjs) twice to find the exact bold-group tag placement rule.

A subagent (68.1-16) ran a prohibited `git stash push` on a shared ref across worktrees, leaving a stray stash entry that had to be carefully identified and dropped without touching the user's own pre-existing stashes; a second subagent (68.1-24) and a third (68.1-30) each separately violated the same no-stash rule mid-session (caught and self-corrected each time).

Two agents (68.1-planner for 68.1-33, and the 68.1-29 exit-gate agent earlier) died on account session-limit resets mid-task, once losing an uncommitted PLAN.md that had to be manually validated and committed by the orchestrator.
A watchdog script polled a `.last-run.json` path that the actual playwright config never wrote to, silently failing to catch a lost wake until the user asked for a status update.

full-workflow.spec.ts 3.9 failed only when run as part of the full suite but passed 53/53 in isolation — an order-dependent race requiring extra root-causing (ultimately a spec-side race, fixed via editing the spec itself, commit 516cd0ee3).
open_items: recovery.html only accepts legacy v2 vault blobs/metadata; the app has produced v3/node-v3 since Phase 62 — needs its own gap-closure plan (user-deferred).
rotation-durability SC-4's relay-replay simulation is unreachable because the API's DB-cache resolve is canonical — needs an apps/api architectural decision or test redesign (user-deferred).

bin restore-to-a-different-parent (not the shipped restore-to-original-parent flow) shares the same orphaned-WriteChildRef bug class as the fixed move path — documented as a safe-for-now follow-up, not fixed.
Files uploaded before the fileReadKey seal fix have permanently mis-sealed refs in the dev vault and will keep failing to decrypt — data damage, not a code bug, needs manual dev-data cleanup.
Codebase drift gate flagged 143 structural elements since the last codebase mapping — advisory, recommends running /gsd-map-codebase.
Commits 17e4319a6/7209e8777 have parens beyond the allowed scope in their subjects — flagged to keep out of the eventual PR title.

Final closing full-suite tally for phase 68.1 (post plan 33) was still being extracted/verified when the transcript ends — phase closeout report and final verifier rescoring not yet delivered to the user.
